item.title: Policy Internship (Fall 2026)
item.description:
Active Minds is the nation's leading nonprofit organization changing the culture around mental health, with a presence at more than 800 high school and college campuses, in corporate settings, and with a wide public audience. Founded in 2003 by Alison Malmon after the death of her brother Brian, Active Minds works to make mental health as highly valued as physical health through programs such as the Send Silence Packing traveling exhibit and Active Minds Speakers. As a small nonprofit, Active Minds relies heavily on its interns, who work directly on important initiatives while gaining experience in the nonprofit sector. This Fall 2026 Policy Internship supports the organization's policy and advocacy work, offering hands-on experience in policy, coalition-building, advocacy, and youth engagement, working directly with the Policy Director on day-to-day operations and strategic initiatives.

Key responsibilities include: taking notes during meetings, webinars, and coalition calls and managing follow-up action items; providing administrative support to the Policy Director, including scheduling and correspondence; attending and helping coordinate meetings, coalition calls, action alerts, and webinars; supporting engagement with youth and young adults interested in advocacy and policy work; contributing to the newsletter, including drafting and compiling content; and supporting other policy and advocacy projects as they arise. Interns are included in meetings, debriefs, and calls to learn the policy process firsthand.

Qualifications: all applicants must be currently enrolled in, or have previously attended, a U.S.-based college or university; an interest in public policy, advocacy, and/or youth engagement; strong written and verbal communication skills; detail orientation with solid organizational and note-taking abilities; the ability to manage multiple tasks and follow through independently; and comfort working with diverse stakeholders, including young people. Applicants must be able to complete a work authorization (I-9) during onboarding.

Compensation and logistics: the internship pays $18 per hour. All Fall 2026 internships are remote, with an anticipated start of September 14, 2026 and end of December 4, 2026. Interns work a minimum of 20 hours per week on a consistent schedule between 9:00am and 5:00pm EST, Monday-Friday, and commit to the full semester. The application window is June 24 through July 8, 2026.

item.description:

Merchant McIntyre & Associates is a midsize federal grants and government relations firm headquartered in Washington, DC, that helps nonprofit clients in higher education, healthcare, and local government reach their federal funding and advocacy goals. This internship supports the firm's client work across legislative tracking, federal grant writing, and long-term policy research.

Key responsibilities include: tracking and researching federal legislation and regulations — including budget proposals and annual appropriations — that impact the firm's clients, using online databases and news sources and attending meetings and briefings on Capitol Hill and with executive agency staff; supporting federal grant writing and legislative/policy objectives, including researching and identifying federal grant opportunities and synthesizing detailed federal grant documents and procurement regulations; conducting long-term research projects across issue areas such as health care, higher education, economic development, and workforce development; compiling reports and client briefing/background materials; performing administrative tasks and coordinating logistics; and supporting the business development team as needed.

Qualifications: recent undergraduates or students currently enrolled in a graduate degree program (relevant programs such as public policy or law preferred); strong research skills, keen attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines; prior experience in a relevant field; and impeccable written and oral communication skills. Applicants must be available to work a minimum of 24 hours per week, with additional availability preferred.

Compensation and logistics: this is a hybrid role in Washington, DC, requiring in-office attendance on Tuesday, Wednesday, and/or Thursday depending on the agreed schedule; remote candidates will not be considered. Applicants submit a resume, two writing samples, and a 250-word response to a prompt about embodying the firm's "essential virtues" (hungry, humble, and smart with people) in lieu of a cover letter.

item.description:

CleanCapital is a diversified clean energy company focused on the middle-market solar and storage industry, mission-driven to mitigate the climate crisis through investments in early-stage, new construction, and operating renewables projects. The company has invested $1.5 billion to date and has acquired and managed over 230 operating and new construction projects across 26 states and one U.S. territory. The Policy & Market Development Intern works with the Policy and Market Development team to shape and track policy changes affecting the development and financing of commercial and community solar and energy storage projects, analyzing market opportunities and tracking federal and state energy policy and regulatory updates.

Key responsibilities include: participating in and taking comprehensive notes on industry calls with an eye toward action items and development opportunities; tracking, analyzing, and communicating federal and state-level regulatory dockets, pending legislation, and stakeholder working groups to understand state solar and energy storage markets; creating detailed summaries and regular reports of state and federal solar policy developments; researching energy markets, renewable energy credit markets, and state programs; supporting the project acquisition and development team in analyzing how policy issues impact deal valuation; and representing the company before industry associations, government officials, and other external engagements.

Qualifications: in pursuit of a BS/BA in political science, economics, environmental studies, engineering, or a related field; interest in the utility/energy industry and in interpreting regulatory and legislative documents; knowledge of policy and regulatory matters pertaining to distributed energy resources (solar, community solar, battery storage); ability to develop data-driven market insights; and strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. Familiarity with project finance concepts and policy-tracking software is preferred.

Compensation and logistics: the range for this position is $31-$41 per hour. The role is fully remote, with the option of a hybrid schedule for those near CleanCapital's NYC or Buffalo offices or in the DC area.

item.title: Trade Policy Internship – Fall 2026 (Paid)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/24/2026.

The American Action Forum (AAF) is a forward-looking, nonprofit policy institute that promotes common-sense, innovative, solutions-based policies to reform government and create a smaller, smarter government. As a fast-paced "action tank," AAF uses modern communications tools to deploy ideas, engage Americans in debate over government policy and market incentives, and educate the media. This paid internship is in AAF's trade policy issue area, reporting directly to Trade Policy Analyst Jacob Jensen, whose research focuses on international trade, the economic impacts of tariff and non-tariff barriers, industrial policy, analysis of congressional trade bills, and the economic power of the BRICS countries.

Key responsibilities include: providing research assistance and data collection for the issue area director; attending Capitol Hill hearings, private speaker events, and events at other DC think tanks to analyze and report on the information presented; helping promote, run, and evaluate AAF events; and creating a semester portfolio and giving a brief presentation on a topic of choice. Example projects completed by prior interns include researching and writing trade policy primers, blogs and op-eds, compiling a trade research database, and writing in-depth papers.

Qualifications: a prerequisite of at least one macroeconomics and one microeconomics course; strong Excel skills (R or Stata a bonus); excellent writing ability and communication skills; an interest in the politics and policies of center-right conservatives; a self-starting attitude; and strong quantitative skills (highly desired).

Compensation and logistics: interns must be available to work 20 to 29 hours per week in person in Washington, DC, and will earn an hourly wage; this is a part-time, paid internship for which interns use their own computer/equipment. Applicants submit a resume, cover letter, and a writing sample of fewer than 1,000 words.

item.description:
CrowdStrike is a global leader in cybersecurity, on a mission to stop breaches with an AI-native security platform. Its University Recruiting program offers paid positions for students and recent grads. This Intelligence Internship sits within CrowdStrike's Counter Adversary Operations team and involves hands-on experience collecting and analyzing data shared on the cybercriminal underground that could impact the security and privacy of CrowdStrike customers and their users.

Key responsibilities include: supporting a wide variety of data collection activities across multiple source types and collection methods; building and maintaining automated collection pipelines leveraging APIs and web scraping across open and closed sources; configuring and managing collection tooling for reliable data acquisition; and conducting and evaluating open-source research and exploratory data analysis on cybersecurity topics supporting CrowdStrike customers.

Qualifications: currently enrolled in a 4-year university with at least 1-2 years of study remaining after the internship, graduating in 2027 or 2028, working toward a degree in computer science, computer engineering, information security, intelligence studies, cybersecurity, cybersecurity policy, international relations, math, physics, or a related field; proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, or analytical languages such as SQL or R; hands-on experience with AI-assisted coding tools; and functional or professional fluency in one or more of Chinese (Mandarin or Cantonese, strongly preferred), Korean (strongly preferred), Spanish (strongly preferred), Arabic, or Farsi. Bonus points for interest in cybersecurity, OSINT tooling knowledge, and command-line tooling.

item.title: CFR Internship Program – Fall 2026
item.description:
Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, headquartered in New York with an office in Washington, DC, dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR publishes Foreign Affairs and maintains the award-winning CFR.org. Through its Blavatnik Internship Program and Robina Franklin Williams Internship Program, CFR offers one of the foremost paid internships in the foreign policy arena, with training in foreign policy and international affairs as well as skills training in writing, research, and program planning. Applicants select the teams they are most interested in interning with.

Key responsibilities include: assisting CFR staff, including preparing relevant briefing materials; performing research as directed using approved CFR databases; writing, reviewing, and editing CFR content; supporting staff on administrative matters and working cross-departmentally as needed; and supporting meetings and events under the direct supervision of CFR staff. Specific duties vary by the individual internship team selected.

Qualifications: an enrolled undergraduate or graduate student; interest in and knowledge of current foreign policy issues preferred; completion of the equivalent of four semesters of college coursework (not including high school AP classes) by the start of the internship; excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills; outstanding written and verbal communication; and strong attention to detail. Specific requirements, including language requirements, vary by team.

Compensation and logistics: interns are paid $18.50 per hour and intern in person in the New York or Washington, DC office about 14-18 hours per week, though some positions may be open to a remote intern. All internships are paid (no exceptions), so all interns must have the legal right to work in the United States. A complete application consists of a resume and one general cover letter; applications are received until July 9, 2026.

item.description:
The Joint Budget Committee (JBC) of the Colorado General Assembly is made up of six elected members of the state legislature tasked with developing the annual state budget. The JBC Staff is a nonpartisan legislative agency that provides objective research, analysis, and recommendations to help the JBC and the legislature write the state budget. This internship offers a unique and rewarding opportunity to contribute to public policy. The office is seeking two part-time assistants to support its work reviewing the management, operations, and fiscal needs of state agencies.

Key responsibilities include: reviewing the management, operations, and fiscal needs of state agencies to develop recommendations for the JBC; developing issue briefs on specified topics impacting state agencies and presenting these issues to the JBC in public meetings; conducting research that informs evidence-based policy choices; and performing administrative tasks within the office.

Qualifications and skills: a background in research, data analysis, economics, or finance; an interest in public policy, nonpartisan work, and/or budget issues; strong research, writing, and presentation skills; and experience with Excel, Google Suite, and/or other databases. Preferred qualifications include a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, coursework in public policy and administration or a related field, and an interest in working in state politics and government. Assistants may qualify for course credit based on institutional requirements.

Compensation and logistics: assistants are compensated at $22.00 per hour plus a $10.00 per day travel stipend, working 20 hours per week between 8:00am and 5:00pm Monday-Friday. This is an in-person position in Denver, CO, from September 14, 2026 through December 18, 2026, with potential to extend through mid-May 2027. Priority consideration is given to applicants who apply before July 10, 2026; the position remains open until filled (posting closes July 31, 2026). Applicants submit a resume, cover letter, 1-2 page writing sample, and two references.

item.company: Johns Hopkins University School of Government and Policy
item.title: AGI Governance Fellowship
item.description:
The Johns Hopkins University School of Government and Policy (SOGP) has launched the AGI Governance Fellowship, led by Professors Gillian Hadfield, Seth Lazar, and Nicholas Caputo, to shape the next generation of leaders in AGI (artificial general intelligence) governance. The fellowship is an intensive, three-week, in-person program at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in Washington, DC, running Tuesday, September 8 through Friday, September 25, 2026. It is designed as a capstone program for early-career researchers and practitioners who already have foundations in AI governance — not an entry point into the field.

The program offers an elite course in AGI governance, exploring pressing questions at the frontier of the AI transition. After a level-setting session, topics include frontier AI legislation at the state and federal level, building societal resilience amid accelerating AI capabilities, embedding democratic practices into AGI alignment, designing new governing institutions for the age of AGI, and navigating changes in humanity's self-understanding. Fellows engage in a full five-day-per-week program of faculty lectures, seminars, collaborative group work, and engagement with guest speakers drawn from frontier labs, government, academia, and civil society, concluding with group projects that materially contribute to AGI governance.

Eligibility: applicants must have a postgraduate degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience, and should be early career — typically within eight years of receiving their undergraduate degree. They should already have solid foundations in the technical understanding of frontier AI systems and/or AI governance. The cohort is expected to span sectors, including congressional staffers, early-career employees at AGI companies, recent PhD graduates, and nonprofit-sector policy advisors and grantmakers. The program targets a cohort of 20-25 fellows.

Compensation and logistics: travel to DC, accommodation, and meals/incidentals are funded by the fellowship. The program is demanding, requiring significant pre-reading and a full-time commitment for its three-week duration. Applications are rolling, but applying by July 15 ensures full consideration.

item.description:

Key responsibilities include: media relations — identifying key media targets, supporting story pitching, navigating reporter relationships, and monitoring coverage; press materials and messaging — drafting and distributing press releases, media advisories, op-eds, Substack posts, social media guidance, talking points, and press kits; social media content development; event management — organizing and coordinating press events and moderating media interactions; strategic planning and campaign development; and special projects, including coordinating the communications agenda for EPN's "Safer, Not Sicker" campaign.

Qualifications: at least 2–4 years of relevant experience; high productivity in remote environments; strong written and verbal communication; a bachelor's or master's degree in Communications, English, Journalism, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field (or equivalent experience); marketing and development experience including writing pitches and proposals; a self-starter orientation; interest in environmental justice and U.S. environmental and health policy; strong project management; proficiency with Google Docs; and CRM database experience.

item.company: North Carolina State University (NC Clean Energy Technology Center)
item.title: Policy Analyst / Sr. Policy Analyst
item.description:
The North Carolina Clean Energy Technology Center at NC State University advances a sustainable energy economy through education, demonstration, and support for clean energy technologies, practices, and policies. Its Energy Policy & Markets Program conducts objective research and analysis and provides education and technical assistance on energy policy issues nationwide, across topics including renewable energy, distributed energy resources, power decarbonization, grid modernization, transportation and building electrification, energy efficiency, utility business models, and rate design. The Policy Analyst / Sr. Policy Analyst supports this program on projects including the Database of State Incentives for Renewables and Efficiency (DSIRE), the DSIRE Insight project, the Carolinas Development Assistance and Siting Hub (Carolinas DASH), and analysis for various Center reports and publications, and engages with external partners as part of the Center's outreach.

Research and analysis responsibilities include: conducting energy policy research for DSIRE, DSIRE Insight, and other team projects; tracking and analyzing energy policy developments (proposed legislation and regulatory proceedings) in a subset of states, plus federal and local developments as needed; reviewing and updating DSIRE policy and program entries; and developing written resources such as white papers, best-practice or model documents, fact sheets, and blog posts. External engagement responsibilities include: sharing research through presentations, social media, and written analysis; supporting stakeholder engagement and facilitation; developing and maintaining partnerships with nonprofits, public utility commissions, state energy offices, local governments, and utilities; supporting grant proposals and business development; and responding to information requests from policymakers, media, and other stakeholders. The Senior Policy Analyst level adds mentoring of entry-level staff, designing and delivering training (workshops, webinars, stakeholder briefings), serving as co-PI or in a significant role on grant-funded initiatives, leading grant-proposal development, and potentially supervising an intern.

Qualifications: for Policy Analyst, a bachelor's degree in environmental studies, public policy, political science, economics, or a related field, with an introductory understanding of federal, state, and local energy policy and regulation, electricity markets, and utility regulation. For Senior Policy Analyst, the same degree plus two or more years of relevant professional experience (a master's may count as one year) and a demonstrated understanding of clean energy policy and utility regulation, including residential and community solar in North Carolina. Both levels require strong analytical, organizational, and written/oral communication skills, the ability to work independently and as part of a team, excellent attention to detail, and a willingness to travel as needed.

Compensation and logistics: the anticipated hiring range is $61,500–$81,800, commensurate with education, experience, and title, based in Raleigh, NC (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.). The posting opened June 22, 2026, with an anticipated close date of July 7, 2026 (applications continue to be reviewed while the posting is active). Applicants should attach a cover letter, CV/resume, and contact information for three references.

item.description:
Pearson is a global learning company. The Advanced Specialist, Government Relations supports Pearson's US Government Relations (USGR) function by tracking, analyzing, and interpreting state-level legislative and policy developments that impact the business and its strategic priorities. Working closely with senior colleagues, the role delivers clear, timely, well-structured policy materials that inform internal decision-making and external engagement, and partners with internal stakeholders across business units to ensure policy analysis reflects operational realities and supports effective advocacy. It is a highly analytical, detail-oriented role combining legislative tracking, policy research, and stakeholder coordination in a fast-paced regulatory environment.

Responsibilities include: monitoring and tracking state legislative and regulatory activity across assigned policy areas and escalating relevant developments; developing and maintaining policy scorecards and tracking progress against business and Government Relations objectives; reviewing introduced legislation and regulatory proposals and summarizing key provisions, status, and business implications; producing recurring legislative trackers, policy digests, alerts, and summaries; supporting internal briefings by organizing research and preparing written materials; partnering with stakeholders to validate business context and data; responding to requests for background research, bill comparisons, and impact analysis (financial, operational, compliance, and customer); drafting policy-facing materials such as one-pagers, talking points, issue summaries, Q&A documents, comment letters, testimony support, and background memos aligned with USGR positioning; assembling briefing packs and notes for meetings with policymakers; tracking legislative deadlines, hearings, and milestones; contributing to improvements in tracking and documentation processes; and using legislative tracking tools to ensure consistent, high-quality reporting.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, Economics, Education Policy, or a related field; 2–5 years of experience in government relations, public policy, legislative affairs, or policy analysis; hands-on experience with legislative tracking, bill analysis, and policy research; strong writing and editing skills; a good understanding of state legislative processes; the ability to manage multiple priorities to deadline with high accuracy; and strong collaboration skills. Desirable: exposure to education policy or another regulated industry; experience drafting policy or regulatory content (summaries, comparison tables, suggested amendments); familiarity with policy areas such as education funding, assessments, procurement, accountability, data privacy, accessibility, or emerging technology; and experience with legislative tracking tools such as FiscalNote, Quorum, or State Net.

Compensation and logistics: this is a remote role based in the United States, working as part of a distributed Government Relations team, with a full-time salary range of $80,000–$100,000 plus annual incentive eligibility and benefits.
